stories.body: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin ended their trilateral summit in Shenzhen with a declaration supporting strategic stability, UN reform and increased oil supplies, but no mention of the wars in Ukraine or Iran. They reaffirmed that nuclear war must never be fought, without agreeing an arms-reduction framework. The statement also challenged the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and emphasized state officials' immunity, a significant issue for Putin, who faces an ICC arrest warrant over the deportation of Ukrainian children. Analysts described the meeting as stronger on symbolism than concrete results, while US-China trade tensions remained unresolved.
stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin issue peace declaration without addressing Ukraine or Iran wars

stories.body: The International Court of Justice ruled by nine votes to six that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during its 2017 military campaign, becoming the first state found responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 convention. At least 10,000 people were killed, and more than a million refugees now live in Bangladesh. The court ordered compensation, with terms to be determined later. Its judgment retained the existing standard for proving genocidal intent while clarifying how intent can be inferred from a state's actions, giving the ruling potential significance for other cases, including South Africa's case against Israel. Bangladesh, The Gambia and the UN secretary general welcomed the decision and urged compliance.
stories.headline: ICJ finds Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya

stories.body: European leaders meeting with Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys in Berlin said they were ready to join negotiations with Russia, while insisting on a neutral venue rather than accepting Putin's invitation to Moscow. US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia had accepted European participation and was comfortable with NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine, but Zelensky and European leaders were more cautious about Moscow's willingness to compromise. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said multilateral talks could take place soon, possibly in the United Arab Emirates. Emmanuel Macron called for faster deliveries of air-defence systems and urged allies to reconsider Ukraine's NATO membership.
stories.headline: Europe presses for a place in Ukraine peace talks and faster air-defence deliveries

stories.body: Anthropic ended its first trading day on Nasdaq up 17%, at just over $97 a share, after raising $81 billion in what the reports describe as the largest IPO in history. The Claude developer became the first frontier generative AI laboratory to go public, but its strong debut failed to lift the wider technology sector. Wall Street closed sharply lower, followed by steep falls in Asian markets on Friday, with Taiwan's benchmark dropping more than 6.5% and South Korea's more than 5% during trading. Investors remain concerned about elevated valuations and whether enormous spending on AI infrastructure will generate sufficient profits.
stories.headline: Anthropic shares rise 17% on debut as broader AI sell-off continues

stories.body: A new COP31 negotiating draft removes references to moving away from fossil fuels, along with a proposed roadmap for that transition and a target to triple adaptation finance to at least $120 billion. Published little more than a day before the scheduled close, the text retains a goal of electrifying 35% of global energy demand by 2035 but does not specify that the electricity should come from renewable sources. The changes follow resistance from oil-producing countries. EU climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said European support would depend on whether the final agreement advances climate action and addresses warming beyond 1.5°C.
stories.headline: COP31 draft drops fossil-fuel transition language and adaptation funding target

stories.body: An early trial involving 61 people with newly diagnosed metastatic pancreatic cancer found that daraxonrasib combined with chemotherapy stopped tumour growth in almost all participants, with cancer becoming undetectable on scans in about one in 12. The drug blocks RAS signalling that drives many pancreatic cancers. Researchers reported deeper responses and longer disease control than typically seen with treatment, but stressed that the results do not establish a cure or prove a survival benefit. Patients had been followed for an average of around 18 months, and longer studies are needed to determine how durable the responses are.
stories.headline: Early pancreatic cancer trial shows promising responses to pill and chemotherapy

stories.body: The White House dismissed national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday after a week of disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The administration has faced criticism over its handling of the outages, although officials say the incidents were unrelated.
stories.headline: White House fires national cyber director after widespread technology outages

stories.body: A Trump administration proposal to change automatic enrollment rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program could reduce benefits for millions of families and threaten access to free school meals for 1.7 million children. The change remains a proposal.
stories.headline: Proposed SNAP change threatens free school meals for 1.7 million children

stories.body: Senate Republicans resisted Trump's request to bypass Democrats on a Pentagon funding bill. Majority Leader John Thune said Republicans would instead try to negotiate an agreement to pass the spending package.
stories.headline: Senate Republicans resist Trump's push for party-line defence funding

stories.body: A cyberattack on third-party vendors may have exposed customer data associated with Chase Bank and Mastercard. Chase said the attack was unrelated to a service disruption on Tuesday; the supplied report does not establish the extent of any exposure.
stories.headline: Vendor cyberattack may have exposed Chase and Mastercard customer data

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez and Alberto Núñez Feijóo faced each other in the campaign's only televised debate before Spain's November 29 election. Feijóo attacked the government's corruption record, while Sánchez apologized for trusting people he should not have and defended his economic and social policies. RTVE's fact-checkers rejected Feijóo's claim that the PSOE faced two irregular-financing cases. On housing, Sánchez advocated more construction alongside market regulation, while Feijóo emphasized building and tax cuts. Sánchez also proposed keeping the minimum wage at 60% of the average wage. The election could put Vox in a position to enter government.
stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo clash over corruption, housing and taxes in election debate

stories.body: Rail unions and Spain's transport ministry agreed a nationwide extreme-weather protocol that provides for service suspensions under red weather alerts and gives drivers explicit authority to stop when they face serious and imminent danger. The agreement expands advance weather information to 48–72 hours and adds hourly accumulated-rainfall data. Adif is identifying vulnerable stretches of track and installing sensors, with further provisions planned for wildfire risks. The measures follow demands for clearer safety rules after fatal rail accidents. Despite progress on this issue, the drivers' union SEMAF maintained its nationwide Renfe strike planned for Monday, November 23.
stories.headline: Rail unions and ministry agree extreme-weather safety protocol as strike remains planned

stories.body: Spain's government plans to approve new environmental and digital-security rules for data centres at an extraordinary cabinet meeting on Friday, ahead of the November 29 election. The revised proposal gives facilities above 10 megawatts five years to obtain 80% of their electricity from renewable sources and allows the grid operator to order disconnections when necessary to protect the electricity system. Earlier drafts covered smaller facilities and imposed tougher requirements. Industry association SpainDC, whose members include Amazon, Google and Microsoft, is preparing a possible Supreme Court challenge, while companies have warned that projects could move to Portugal or southern France.
stories.headline: Spain plans to approve data-centre rules despite industry opposition

stories.body: The Generalitat has set minimum Rodalies services for Monday, November 23, at 66% of trains during peak periods, from 6:00 to 9:30 a.m. and 5:00 to 8:30 p.m., and 33% during the rest of the day. Renfe is notifying assigned drivers by email and hand-delivered letters after disputes over notifications and failures to operate all minimum services during previous strikes. SEMAF's planned 24-hour walkout also affects regional and high-speed Renfe services across Spain. Negotiations continue, but the union says outstanding safety commitments have not yet been fully implemented.
stories.headline: Monday's Rodalies strike has minimum services of 66% at peak times

stories.body: Barcelona has approved a permanent expansion of its street-cleaning and rubbish-collection contract, adding 57 teams and 99 workers at an annual cost of €23.5 million. The increase brings the daily workforce to 2,115 and responds to new public spaces and heavier use of existing streets, parks and green corridors. The changes include 16 additional neighbourhood brigades, with particular emphasis on Nou Barris and Horta-Guinardó, more cleaning of planted areas, and greater capacity to remove waste left beside bins. Additional pavement scrubbing will serve squares in Sants-Montjuïc, Les Corts and Sarrià-Sant Gervasi.
stories.headline: Barcelona adds 99 workers and €23.5 million a year to cleaning services

stories.body: TMB has introduced a quiet-hours pilot at the Punt TMB customer-service centre in the L5 concourse at Sagrada Família station for autistic people and passengers with sensory sensitivities. On working weekdays from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m., the centre will reduce lighting, limit digital screens and non-essential announcements, minimize disruptive tasks and provide sensory support materials. Staff have received training in autism, sensory sensitivity and accessible communication. Passengers can still receive assistance during normal opening hours, and feedback from the pilot will help determine whether the scheme expands to other customer-service points.
stories.headline: TMB trials quiet hours at Sagrada Família customer-service point

stories.body: A Barcelona municipal committee unanimously granted provisional planning approval to restore the nine surviving houses of Colònia Castells on Passatge Piera for public use. The 354 square metres will accommodate a local-history space, a multipurpose meeting room, premises for neighbourhood groups and storage for community-garden tools. The plan gives the gardens a permanent location and creates a 30-metre-wide green connection to the Gaietà Renom gardens. It also expands the grounds available to Paideia, a school serving pupils with disabilities, by 396 square metres to incorporate its playground and sports court.
stories.headline: Barcelona provisionally approves community uses for Colònia Castells' nine surviving houses
